clues.text: I was a son of Gideon.
I killed 70 of Gideon's sons on one stone, but Jotham hid and survived.
The leaders of Shechem made me king.
A woman dropped an upper millstone on my head and crushed my skull.
I asked my attendant to strike me down so that people would not say, 'A woman killed him.'
My mother's brothers persuaded the leaders of Shechem to support me as their own relative.
I used 70 pieces of silver from the house of Baal-berith to hire idle and insolent men.
I ruled over Israel for three years.
I captured Shechem, pulled the city down, and sowed it with salt.
After Zebul warned me about Gaal's revolt, I used four bands in an ambush against Shechem.
My surviving brother compared me to a bramble whose fire could consume the cedars of Lebanon.
The leaders who made me king later posted men on the mountaintops to ambush me.
My father refused a request that he and his sons rule Israel, but after his death I was made king.
I burned Shechem's leaders in the vault of the house of El-berith.
After burning about 1,000 people in one tower, I tried to burn another tower and was fatally injured there.
Joab referred to my death when speaking about the danger of fighting too close to a city wall.
I was a daughter of Caleb.
I became the wife of Othniel after he captured Kiriath-sepher.
My father gave me land in the south.
I urged Othniel to ask my father for a field.
I dismounted from my donkey when my father asked what I wanted.
I asked Caleb for springs of water, and he gave me Upper Gulloth and Lower Gulloth.
I was found in Bezek when Judah fought the Canaanites and Perizzites.
I fled but was caught, and my thumbs and big toes were cut off.
Seventy kings whose thumbs and big toes I had cut off picked up food under my table.
I said that God had repaid me for what I had done.
I was brought to Jerusalem, where I died.
I was king of the Amalekites.
I was caught alive by Saul.
I was hacked to pieces by Samuel at Gilgal.
I went to Samuel reluctantly when he summoned me.
I had been saying to myself that the threat of death was past.
I was spared along with the best of the flock, the herd, the fattened animals, and the rams.
I was summoned when Samuel said, "Bring the king of Amalek near to me."
Saul claimed that the animals spared along with me were intended for sacrifice to Jehovah.
I was spared by an enemy king while the rest of my people were killed with the sword.
I was told that just as my sword had bereaved women of children, my mother would be most bereaved among women.
My people had been ordered devoted to destruction, with none to be spared.
My people were struck down from Havilah as far as Shur, next to Egypt.
From my people, only the worthless goods were devoted to destruction; what was good was spared with me.
My city was approached with an ambush by the valley.
The Kenites living among my people were told to leave so they would not be swept away with us.
I was the captive Saul pointed to when claiming he had obeyed Jehovah.
I died after Samuel said that to obey is better than a sacrifice.
My people were attacked to call them to account for opposing Israel on the way up from Egypt.
Sparing me and the best of the spoil led to Saul being rejected as king.
My people were involved in the disobedience that led Jehovah to say he regretted making Saul king.
After I was spared, Samuel cried out to Jehovah all night.
After my people were defeated, a monument was erected for Saul at Carmel.
I fought alongside Deborah against Sisera.
Jehovah threw Sisera and all his war chariots and army into confusion before my sword.
I sang a victory song with Deborah.
I was told Jehovah would bring Sisera to the stream of Kishon and give him into my hand.
I said that if Deborah went with me I would go, but if she did not go with me I would not go.
I chased Sisera's war chariots and army as far as Harosheth of the nations.
I descended from Mount Tabor only after Deborah said it was the day Jehovah would give Sisera into my hand.
I left not even one of Sisera's army remaining after the chase.
I was told my campaign would not bring me glory, because Jehovah would give Sisera into the hand of a woman.
I led 10,000 men down from Mount Tabor.
I summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh.
I was told to march to Mount Tabor with 10,000 men of Naphtali and Zebulun.
I went to Jael's tent in pursuit of Sisera and found him lying dead with a tent pin through his temples.
I was met by Jael, who offered to show me the man I was looking for.
I pursued Sisera's army while he got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
I was reported to Sisera as having gone up to Mount Tabor.
In the victory song it was said that into the valley plain I was sent on foot.
I pursued Sisera's chariots while he fled on foot to Jael's tent, where a woman killed him before I arrived.
I was the son of Abinoam.
I was sent for out of Kedesh-naphtali.
I faced an army that included 900 chariots with iron scythes.
In the victory song I was called to rise up and lead my captives away as the son of my father.
I was later listed among those who through faith defeated kingdoms.
After my battle, Jabin the king of Canaan was subdued before the Israelites.
I was king of Mesopotamia.
Israel served me for eight years.
Jehovah gave Israel into my hand after they did what was bad in His eyes.
I was defeated by Othniel, the son of Kenaz.
Jehovah raised Othniel up as a savior to rescue Israel from me.
Jehovah gave me into Othniel's hand when he went out to battle.
My rule followed Israel's service to the Baals and sacred poles.
After I was defeated, the land had rest for 40 years.
I was the oppressor defeated before Othniel died and before Israel served Eglon of Moab.
I was a prophetess who judged Israel.
I summoned Barak to fight Sisera.
I went with Barak to Kedesh.
I sang a song with Barak on the day of the victory.
I received Israelites who came up to me for judgment.
I told Barak Jehovah had commanded him to take 10,000 men of Naphtali and Zebulun to Mount Tabor.
I told Barak that Jehovah would give Sisera into the hand of a woman.
My palm tree was in the mountainous region of Ephraim.
I told Barak that if he would not go without me, I would certainly go with him.
I prophesied that Barak's campaign would not bring him glory.
A Kenite woman fulfilled my prophecy that Sisera would fall to a woman.
I was the wife of Lappidoth.
I sat under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel.
I told Barak Jehovah would bring Sisera to the stream of Kishon.
I said to Barak, "Rise up, for this is the day that Jehovah will give Sisera into your hand."
In my song I said I arose as a mother in Israel.
In my song I said the villagers in Israel were no more until I rose up.
In my song I said that from heaven the stars fought against Sisera.
In my song I said the torrent of Kishon washed Sisera's forces away.
In my song I called Jael most blessed of women.
I judged Israel while Jabin harshly oppressed the people for 20 years with 900 chariots with iron scythes.
After the victory I shared in, the land had rest for 40 years.
I said in a song that in the days of Shamgar and Jael the roads were deserted.
I said an angel of Jehovah cursed Meroz because its inhabitants did not come to Jehovah's assistance.
In a song I described Sisera's mother peering out from a lattice and asking why his chariot was delayed.
I said Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to the point of death.
In a song I asked why Reuben sat down between the two saddlebags listening to pipes for the flocks.
I was the woman Samson fell in love with.
I learned the secret of a man who loved me so that I could betray him to the Philistines.
I lived in the Valley of Sorek.
I asked someone what gave him his great power.
I was offered 1,100 silver pieces by each of the Philistine lords to find out how a man could be subdued.
After I had a Nazirite's hair shaved, he did not know that Jehovah had left him.
I tied a man who loved me, with seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried out.
I called out, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!"
I tied someone with new ropes that had not been used for work.
I wove the seven braids of a man's head with the warp thread.
I made a man who loved me fall asleep on my knees.
I told someone he had fooled me and told me lies.
I was fooled three times before a man who loved me opened his heart to me.
Because I kept nagging someone day after day, he was weary to the point of dying.
I asked how the man who loved me could say his heart was not with me.
I fixed someone's braids with a pin, but he woke and pulled out the loom pin and the warp thread.
I summoned the Philistine lords when the man who loved me finally opened his heart to me.
I called a man and had him shave off the seven braids of another man's head.
I tested the power of a man I was trying to bind while Philistine men waited in ambush in the inner room.
I learned that a man was a Nazirite of God from birth and that a razor had never touched his head.
After I betrayed a man, his eyes were bored out and he was bound with two copper fetters.
When I tied a man with bowstrings, he tore them apart as easily as a thread of flax comes apart when it touches fire.
When I tied a man with new ropes, he tore them off his arms like threads.
I received the Philistine lords who came bringing the money after a man who loved me opened his heart.
I began to have control over a Nazirite after his hair was shaved, for his power was leaving him.
I was king of Moab in the days of the Judges.
I was a very fat man.
I received tribute from Israel through Ehud.
I was killed by a left-handed Benjaminite.
I dismissed my attendants after Ehud said he had a secret message for me.
I rose up from my throne when Ehud said he had a message from God.
Ehud plunged a sword into my belly with his left hand.
My servants waited at the locked doors of my roof chamber, thinking I was relieving myself.
The Israelites served me for 18 years.
I brought the Ammonites and Amalekites against Israel and captured the city of palm trees.
I prevailed over Israel after they again did what was bad in Jehovah's eyes following the death of the son of Kenaz.
My death led to Israel capturing the fords of the Jordan and striking down about 10,000 Moabites.
After I was killed, Moab was subdued and the land had rest for 80 years.
I was the son of Gera.
I was a left-handed Benjaminite.
I killed Eglon, the king of Moab.
I made a two-edged sword a cubit long.
I delivered Israel's tribute to Eglon.
I strapped my sword underneath my garment on my right thigh.
I told Eglon I had a secret message for him.
I told Eglon I had a message from God for him.
I came to Eglon while he was sitting alone in his cool roof chamber.
I presented tribute to a very fat king.
I was a Benjaminite whom Jehovah raised up as a savior of Israel.
I drew my sword from my right thigh with my left hand and plunged it into Eglon's belly.
I locked the doors of the roof chamber behind me after killing the king of Moab.
I escaped while Eglon's servants thought he was relieving himself behind locked doors.
The handle of my sword went in after the blade, and the fat closed in over it.
After I presented the tribute, I sent away the people who had carried it, then later returned alone.
I waited until Eglon's attendants left him after he said, "Silence!"
I escaped while Eglon's servants lingered, and I made it safely to Seirah.
I passed by the carved images at Gilgal both when returning to a Moabite king and when escaping.
I sounded the horn in the mountainous region of Ephraim, and the Israelites followed me.
I led Israel to capture the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites so that no one could cross.
Under my lead, Israel struck down about 10,000 Moabites, all strong and valiant men; not a single one escaped.
After I helped subdue Moab, the land had rest for 80 years.
I was raised up as a savior after Israel had served Eglon for 18 years.
Before I delivered Israel, Eglon had brought the Ammonites and Amalekites against us and captured the city of palm trees.
I said to Israel, "Follow me, because Jehovah has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand."
I was raised up as a savior of Israel after Othniel.
After me was Shamgar, son of Anath, who also saved Israel.
I was a priest in Shiloh.
I was the father of Hophni and Phinehas.
I judged Israel for 40 years.
I thought Hannah was drunk while she was praying.
I blessed Hannah, asking the God of Israel to grant her petition.
I blessed Elkanah and Hannah after they lent their son to Jehovah.
I heard reports that my sons were doing bad things to all Israel.
I rebuked my sons for lying down with the women serving at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
I realized that Jehovah was calling Samuel and taught him how to answer.
I asked Samuel not to hide a single word of the message Jehovah gave him.
I fell backward from my seat when I heard that the Ark had been captured.
I said, “It is Jehovah. Let him do what is good in his eyes.”
I was very old when I heard about the wrongdoing of my sons.
A man of God told me that I honored my sons more than Jehovah.
I was told that both of my sons would die on the same day as a sign against my house.
My neck was broken when I fell backward from my seat beside the gate.
I was told that the error of my house would never be atoned for by sacrifices or offerings.
My heart trembled over the Ark of the true God while I sat by the roadside watching.
I was 98 years old and could not see when news arrived from the battle line.
My daughter-in-law went into labor when she heard that I, her husband, and the Ark had been lost.
I was Hannah's husband.
I had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah.
I went up to Shiloh year after year to worship and sacrifice to Jehovah.
I was Samuel's father.
Samuel's mother was the one I loved.
I gave portions of a sacrifice to Peninnah and all her sons and daughters, but a special portion to Hannah.
I asked my wife whether I was not better to her than ten sons.
I went up with all my household to offer the yearly sacrifice and my vow offering.
I agreed when Hannah said she would bring our son to remain before Jehovah after he was weaned.
I received Eli's blessing that Jehovah would grant Hannah another child in place of the one lent to Him.
I was the son of Jeroham and a descendant of Zuph.
I told Hannah to stay home until she had weaned our son.
I bowed before Jehovah with my household before returning to Ramah.
I had relations with my wife after we returned home from Shiloh, and Jehovah gave attention to her.
I lived in Ramathaim-zophim in the mountainous region of Ephraim.
After my son was lent to Jehovah, I had three more sons and two daughters through my favourite wife.
I was from the mountainous region of Ephraim, although my genealogy traces through Zuph.
I was the son of Ebed.
I crossed over into Shechem with my brothers.
The leaders of Shechem put their trust in me.
I cursed Abimelech while eating and drinking in the house of a god.
I challenged the people of Shechem to stop serving Abimelech.
I said that I would depose Abimelech if the people were under my command.
I challenged Abimelech to increase his army and come out.
When Zebul the prince of Shechem heard my words against Abimelech, his anger blazed.
Zebul secretly warned Abimelech that I and my brothers were inciting Shechem against him.
Zebul said that I was seeing the shadows of the mountains as if they were men.
I went out to fight Abimelech at the head of the leaders of Shechem.
I fled from Abimelech and many men fell slain near the entrance of the city gate of Shechem.
Zebul drove my brothers and me out of Shechem after Abimelech pursued me.
I led 300 men against the Midianites.
I used horns, large jars, and torches to defeat the Midianites.
I tore down my father's altar of Baal and cut down its sacred pole.
I kept only the 300 men who lapped water by putting their hand to their mouth.
I divided my 300 men into three bands.
I asked God for signs involving a fleece and dew.
I was called a mighty warrior by Jehovah's angel.
I said my clan was the least in Manasseh and I was the most insignificant in my father's house.
I built an altar and called it Jehovah-shalom.
My father gave me a new name after I pulled down Baal's altar.
I sounded the horn and the Abiezrites rallied behind me.
I sent messengers through Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali to gather men.
I was beating out wheat in a winepress to hide it from Midian.
I prepared a young goat, unleavened bread, and broth for Jehovah's angel.
Fire flared up from a rock and consumed the food I had brought to Jehovah's angel.
I feared my father's household and the men of the city, so I tore down Baal's altar at night.
I tested my men by sending home those who were afraid and trembling.
I went down to the Midianite camp with Purah, my attendant.
I heard a dream about a round loaf of barley bread that overturned a Midianite tent.
I told my men to watch me and do exactly what I did.
I asked the men of Succoth for loaves of bread while I chased Zebah and Zalmunna.
My concubine in Shechem bore me a son whom I named Abimelech.
I captured Zebah and Zalmunna after attacking their camp while it was off guard.
I killed Zebah and Zalmunna after they said they had killed my brothers at Tabor.
I refused Israel's request that I, my son, and my grandson rule over them.
I was the son of Joash the Abiezrite.
I calmed the men of Ephraim by comparing their gleanings with the grape harvest of Abiezer.
I made an ephod from 1,700 gold shekels of nose rings and displayed it in Ophrah.
The ephod I made became a snare to my household after all Israel committed idolatry with it.
Midian was subdued in my days, and the land had rest for 40 years.
I became father to 70 sons because I had many wives.
I was told that I would strike down Midian as if they were one man.
Jehovah reduced my army so Israel could not claim that its own hand had saved it.
After I heard the Midianite dream and its interpretation, I bowed down to worship before returning to my camp.
The 300 men with me stood in their places while Jehovah turned the Midianites' swords against one another.
I was Samuel's mother.
I prayed for a son and named him Samuel.
I made a vow to give my son to Jehovah all the days of his life.
I gave Samuel to serve at Jehovah's house after I weaned him.
I was the wife my husband loved.
I had no children while Peninnah had children.
My rival wife taunted me relentlessly, making me weep and not eat.
I was extremely bitter when I began to pray to Jehovah and weep uncontrollably.
I promised that no razor would touch my son's head.
I spoke in my heart while my lips trembled, but my voice was not heard.
I rejoiced in Jehovah in a prayer after lending Samuel to Him.
I told Eli that I was pouring out my soul before Jehovah.
I was mistaken for a drunk woman by the high priest.
I said I was a woman under great stress who had not drunk wine or anything alcoholic.
After Eli blessed me, I went on my way, ate, and my face was no longer downcast.
I said Samuel's name meant that I had asked for him from Jehovah.
I stayed home until Samuel was weaned while Elkanah went to offer the yearly sacrifice.
I brought my son to Shiloh with a three-year-old bull, flour, and wine after he was weaned.
I reminded the high priest that I was the woman who had stood there praying to Jehovah.
I lent my son to Jehovah for all his days.
I made my son a little sleeveless coat and brought it to him year after year.
I said that Jehovah raises the lowly one from the dust and lifts up the poor from the ash heap.
I said that not by power does a man prevail.
I said Jehovah would judge to the ends of the earth and give power to his king.
I said that the barren has given birth to seven, but the woman with many sons has become desolate.
After my first son, I gave birth to three more sons and two daughters.
The high priest asked Jehovah to grant me another child in place of the one I had lent to Him.
I was a son of Eli.
I served as a priest to Jehovah in Shiloh.
I died on the same day as my brother Phinehas.
I was with the Ark of the covenant when it came into Israel's camp.
I treated Jehovah's offering with disrespect.
I was called a wicked man who had no regard for Jehovah.
My attendants demanded raw meat before the fat was made to smoke.
My attendants threatened to take sacrificial meat by force.
My attendants took meat from sacrifices with a three-pronged fork.
I lay down with women serving at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
I refused to listen when my father rebuked me.
I was told that my death with Phinehas on one day would be a sign against my father's house.
My father knew about the judgment coming on his house because of the error that included me.
I died when the Ark of God was captured by the Philistines.
My death, my brother's death, and the capture of the Ark caused my father to fall backward and die.
On the day I died, my father's daughter-in-law went into labor.
I was born when the Ark of the true God was captured.
I was the son of Phinehas.
My mother gave me my name, although hers was not recorded in the Bible.
I was born after my father and grandfather died.
I was born while my mother was dying.
My mother unexpectedly went into labor after hearing that the Ark had been captured.
The women beside my dying mother told her that she had given birth to me, but she did not answer them.
Ahijah, the son of my brother Ahitub, served as priest in Saul's day.
I was the grandson of Eli.
My mother said that glory had gone away from Israel into exile when she named me.
I was born into the household of Eli on the day the Ark was captured and both of his sons died.
My mother named me after hearing of the loss of the Ark, my father, and my grandfather.
My name means “Where Is the Glory?”
I harshly oppressed Israel for 20 years.
Sisera was the chief of my army.
My army had 900 chariots with iron scythes.
God subdued me before Israel after Sisera was killed by Jael.
I was king of Canaan and reigned in Hazor.
Jehovah sold Israel into my hand after they did what was bad in His eyes.
My army was defeated after Deborah sent Barak to Mount Tabor with 10,000 men.
I had peace with the house of Heber the Kenite.
Israel's hand came down harder and harder against me until they destroyed me.
My commander assembled his chariots and troops at the stream of Kishon to fight Israel.
I gave Sisera a drink from a skin bottle of milk when he asked me for water.
I invited Sisera into my tent while he was fleeing on foot.
I covered Sisera with a blanket in my tent.
I drove a tent pin through Sisera's temples and beat it into the ground.
Sisera told me to stand at my tent entrance and say that no man was there.
I took a tent pin and a hammer in my hand while Sisera was asleep and exhausted.
I told Barak that I would show him Sisera.
I fulfilled Deborah's prophecy that Sisera would be given into the hand of a woman.
I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
Barak found Sisera dead in my tent with a tent pin through his temples.
Deborah and Barak's song called me most blessed of women living in tents.
In Deborah and Barak's song, I offered Sisera curdled milk in a majestic banquet bowl.
In a victory song, Sisera was said to have collapsed and fallen between my feet.
There was peace between Jabin of Hazor and the house of my husband.
I killed the commander who fled from a battle in which Jehovah threw his army into confusion.
I was named in the song as a marker of the time when travelers kept to back roads.
My killing a military commander was followed by God's subduing the king of Canaan before Israel.
I was a mighty warrior from Gilead.
I judged Israel for six years.
I made a vow to Jehovah before fighting the Ammonites.
I said that whoever came out of my house to meet me when I returned would become Jehovah's.
My one and only child came out to meet me playing the tambourine and dancing.
I defeated the Ammonites.
I was the son of Gilead and a prostitute.
I was driven out of my father's house by my brothers.
I became leader and commander over the inhabitants of Gilead.
My daughter asked to spend two months in the mountains weeping over her virginity.
Young women in Israel went four days each year to give commendation to my daughter.
I settled in the land of Tob after fleeing from my brothers.
Idle men joined company with me in Tob.
The elders of Gilead brought me back to serve as their commander against Ammon.
I sent messengers to the king of Ammon about his attack on my land.
I told the king of Ammon that Israel had not taken the land of Moab or Ammon.
I said that Israel had lived in Heshbon, Aroer, and the cities by the Arnon for 300 years.
I said that I had not sinned against the Ammonites and called on Jehovah the Judge.
Jehovah's spirit came upon me as I passed through Gilead and Manasseh.
I struck down the Ammonites from Aroer to Minnith, 20 cities, and as far as Abel-keramim.
My daughter never had relations with a man after I carried out the vow regarding her.
I risked my life against Ammon after Ephraim failed to save me.
My men used the word 'Shibboleth' to identify fleeing Ephraimites.
I fought Ephraim after they threatened to burn my house down with me in it.
After my death, I was buried in my city in Gilead.
I was my father's one and only child.
I came out to meet my father with a tambourine and dancing after his victory over the Ammonites.
I told my father to do to me what he had promised Jehovah.
I asked to spend two months in the mountains with my female companions.
I wept over my virginity in the mountains.
I never had relations with a man.
The young women of Israel went four days each year to give me commendation.
I was the youngest son of Jerubbaal.
I survived when Abimelech killed 70 sons of Jerubbaal on one stone.
I fled to Beer and lived there because of Abimelech.
I stood on top of Mount Gerizim and called out to the leaders of Shechem.
I told a parable in which the trees asked the bramble to rule over them.
I challenged the leaders of Shechem over making Abimelech king.
I said that fire should come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo if they had acted dishonorably.
I was Samson's father.
I was a Danite from Zorah.
I pleaded with Jehovah to send the man of the true God again.
My wife was told that our son would be a Nazirite of God from birth.
My wife and I were childless before she gave birth to our son.
I asked what our child's manner of life and work would be.
I went with my wife to meet the man who had spoken to her.
I asked whether he was the man who had spoken to my wife.
I asked Jehovah's angel to stay while we prepared a young goat.
I asked Jehovah's angel for his name so that we could honor him when his words came true.
Jehovah's angel told my wife that no razor should touch our son's head.
Jehovah's angel told my wife that our son would take the lead in saving Israel from the Philistines.
I did not know that a man I spoke with was Jehovah's angel.
I took a young goat and grain offering and offered them on a rock to Jehovah.
I watched Jehovah's angel ascend in the flame from the altar.
My wife and I fell with our faces to the ground after Jehovah's angel ascended in the flame from an altar.
I realized that I had seen Jehovah's angel only after he had left.
My wife reasoned that Jehovah would not have accepted our offering or shown us these things if he intended to put us to death.
I said that we were sure to die because we had seen God.
Jehovah's angel said to me, "Why is it that you ask about my name, seeing that it is a wonderful one?"
Jehovah listened to my plea to send back a visitor, but when he returned to my wife, I was not with her.
The first time I met Jehovah's angel, I asked him what our child's work would be; the angel answered by repeating what my wife was to avoid.
Jehovah's angel did not appear to me again after I realized who he was.
I lived in the mountainous region of Ephraim.
I took 1,100 silver pieces from my mother and later returned them.
I had a house of gods.
I made an ephod and teraphim statues.
I installed one of my sons as priest.
I gave silver back to my mother after hearing the curse she pronounced over it.
My mother used 200 silver pieces to have a silversmith make a carved image and a metal statue.
I hired a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah to serve as my priest.
I offered the Levite ten silver pieces a year, garments, and food.
I said that Jehovah would be good to me because the Levite had become my priest.
The Danites took my carved image, ephod, teraphim statues, metal image, and priest.
I pursued the Danites and asked what I had left after they took my gods and priest.
I turned back to my house because the Danites I pursued were stronger than I was.
The carved image I made remained with the Danites all the days that the house of the true God was in Shiloh.
I was an Ammonite king in the days of King Saul of Israel.
I camped against Jabesh in Gilead.
The men of Jabesh offered to make a covenant with me and serve me.
I would make a covenant with Jabesh only if every man's right eye was bored out.
I said that taking the right eyes of Jabesh would humiliate all Israel.
The elders of Jabesh asked me for seven days to send messengers through Israel.
Saul's army attacked my camp during the morning watch and struck down the Ammonites.
I was the son of Kenaz.
My father was the younger brother of Caleb.
Jehovah raised me up as a savior to rescue Israel when they cried to him for help.
I was the judge raised before Ehud.
Jehovah's spirit came upon me and I became judge of Israel.
I went out to battle against the king of Mesopotamia.
Israel had served the king of Mesopotamia for eight years before Jehovah raised me up.
The land had rest for 40 years after my victory.
My son was named Hathath.
I took up Caleb's challenge to strike Kiriath-sepher (Debir) and capture it.
Caleb gave me his daughter Achsah as a wife.
My wife urged me to ask her father for a field.
Caleb gave my wife Upper Gulloth and Lower Gulloth after she asked for a blessing.
I prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia.
I was the first savior raised up in the book of Judges after Joshua died and Israel served foreign gods.
My descendant was chosen to head a service group of 24,000 during David's reign.
After I died, Israel again did what was bad in Jehovah's eyes, leading to Moab's rule over them.
I taunted my rival relentlessly because she had no children.
I was Hannah's rival wife.
I was one of Elkanah's two wives.
My rivalry with Hannah forms the setting in which she prayed for and later gave birth to Samuel.
Elkanah gave portions of his sacrifice to me and all my children.
I had both sons and daughters.
I had children while my rival, the wife my husband loved, had none at that time.
I went up with my husband's household year after year to worship at Shiloh.
I was a son of Eli.
I served as a priest to Jehovah in Shiloh.
I died on the same day as my brother Hophni.
I was with the Ark of the covenant when it came into Israel's camp.
I was called a wicked man who had no regard for Jehovah.
My attendants took meat from sacrifices with a three-pronged fork.
My attendants demanded raw meat before the fat was made to smoke.
My attendants threatened to take sacrificial meat by force.
I treated Jehovah's offering with disrespect.
I lay down with women serving at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
I refused to listen when my father rebuked me.
I was told that my death with Hophni on one day would be a sign against my father's house.
I died when the Ark of God was captured by the Philistines.
My death and the capture of the Ark caused my wife to go into labor.
My wife named our son Ichabod after the Ark was captured and I died.
My father's house was judged for an error that included the conduct of his sons.
I was a Nazirite of God from birth.
I killed 1,000 Philistines with the jawbone of a donkey.
Delilah betrayed me after I told her the secret of my strength.
No razor was to touch my head.
I found honey in the carcass of a lion and gave some to my parents without telling them where it came from.
Jehovah's spirit empowered me to tear a lion in two like a young goat.
I told Delilah that shaving my head would cause my power to leave me.
I did not tell my parents that I had killed a lion.
I tore down the gates of Gaza and carried them to a mountain facing Hebron.
I killed more Philistines at my death than during my life.
I was the son of Manoah.
I was born after Jehovah's angel appeared to my mother and father.
I wanted a Philistine woman from Timnah as my wife.
I made a riddle about something to eat coming out of an eater, and something sweet out of the strong.
I struck down 30 men at Ashkelon and gave their clothing to men who solved my riddle.
I caught 300 foxes and used torches to burn Philistine grain, vineyards, and olive groves.
I was tied with two new ropes by 3,000 men of Judah.
I judged Israel for 20 years.
My ropes became like scorched linen threads when Jehovah's spirit empowered me at Lehi.
Jehovah's angel told my mother that I would take the lead in saving Israel from the Philistines.
I did not know that Jehovah had left me after the woman I loved had my hair shaved.
I said my riddle-solvers had plowed with my young cow.
My wife was given to one of my groomsmen after I left in anger.
I named a place Ramath-lehi after striking down 1,000 men with a jawbone.
I called on Jehovah when thirsty, and water flowed from a hollow at Lehi.
My eyes were bored out and I became a grinder of grain in prison.
I asked the boy holding my hand to let me feel the pillars supporting the house we were in.
I asked Jehovah to strengthen me just once more so I could take revenge for one of my eyes.
My hair began to grow back after it had been shaved.
I said, “As they did to me, so I did to them,” when the men of Judah questioned me.
I was called out of prison to entertain Philistine worshippers of Dagon.
My parents did not realize that my desire for a Philistine wife was from Jehovah, who was seeking an opportunity against the Philistines.
The Philistines burned my wife and her father after learning that I had burned their crops.
I was captured by my own people before Jehovah's spirit enabled me to defeat the Philistines at Lehi.
About 3,000 men and women watched from a roof while I entertained the Philistines.
I was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of my father.
I was a prophet of Jehovah.
I anointed Saul as king over Israel.
I was the son of Hannah and Elkanah.
I ministered before Jehovah as a boy.
Jehovah called me while I was lying in the temple.
I judged Israel throughout my life.
I wore a linen ephod as a boy.
My mother made me a little sleeveless coat and brought it to me year after year.
I was lent to Jehovah for all my days by my mother.
I ran to Eli three times because I thought he had called me.
I said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
I was afraid to tell Eli the vision Jehovah gave me.
I told Eli everything Jehovah had said and hid nothing from him.
I told Israel to put away foreign gods and Ashtoreth images.
I gathered Israel at Mizpah and prayed to Jehovah for them.
I offered a suckling lamb as a whole burnt offering while Israel faced the Philistines.
I named a stone Ebenezer, saying, “Until now Jehovah has helped us.”
I traveled each year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah to judge Israel.
I built an altar to Jehovah in Ramah, where my house was.
I told Israel that asking for a king was an evil thing in Jehovah's eyes.
I called on Jehovah to make it thunder and rain during the wheat harvest.
I said it would be unthinkable for me to sin against Jehovah by ceasing to pray for Israel.
I was confirmed as Jehovah's prophet by all Israel from Dan to Beer-sheba.
Jehovah did not let any of my words go unfulfilled.
I judged Israel after the Ark had remained at Kiriath-jearim for 20 years.
Jehovah caused loud thunder against the Philistines while I was offering a burnt offering.
The Philistines were subdued and their cities from Ekron to Gath were returned to Israel during my days.
I told Israel that they had rejected Jehovah as their king by demanding a human king.
I warned Israel that a king would take their sons, daughters, fields, servants, herds, and flocks.
I met Saul while he was searching for his father's lost donkeys.
I gave Saul the reserved portion at a meal before telling him Jehovah's word.
I poured oil on Saul's head and told him Jehovah had anointed him as leader.
I called Israel to Mizpah, where Saul was selected while hiding among the luggage.
I asked Israel to testify whether I had taken a bull, a donkey, or a bribe from anyone.
I saved Israel from the Philistines before the time of Samson.
I came after Ehud in the time of the judges.
I was named with Jael in Deborah and Barak's victory song.
I was first mentioned in the Bible immediately after the account of Moab's defeat under Ehud.
I was the son of Anath.
In my days, the roads were deserted and travelers kept to back roads.
I saved Israel after Ehud and before Israel's oppression under Jabin.
My only narrative action was striking down 600 Philistines with a cattle goad.
Deborah's song used my days to describe a time when Israel's roads were deserted.
I was the chief of Jabin's army.
I was killed by Jael with a tent pin.
I fled on foot from Barak's army.
I fled to Jael's tent because there was peace between Jabin and the house of Heber.
I was asleep and exhausted when Jael drove a tent pin through my temples.
I got down from my chariot and fled on foot after Jehovah threw my army into confusion.
I asked Jael for water because I was thirsty, but she gave me milk.
I told Jael to stand at her tent entrance and deny that any man was inside.
In the song, Jael was said to have crushed my head and pierced my temples.
I was defeated when Barak led 10,000 men down Mount Tabor.
I had 900 chariots with iron scythes.
Barak found me dead in a woman's tent with a tent pin through my temples.
Deborah had foretold that I would be given into the hand of a woman.
In Deborah and Barak's song, the stars were said to fight against me from their orbits.
In the song, the torrent of Kishon was said to wash my forces away.
I lived in Harosheth of the nations.
I assembled my chariots and troops at the stream of Kishon.
My mother was described as peering from a lattice and asking why my chariot was delayed.
I led the army that harshly oppressed Israel for 20 years.
I abandoned my chariot and fled on foot to the tent of the woman who later killed me.
Deborah and Barak sang a victory song that pictured my mother waiting for my chariot to return.
In Deborah's song, my mother's attendants expected me to return with embroidered garments and other spoil.
